name: Armenia
snapshot: Nikol Pashinyan won a third term outright in June 2026 on the promise of peace with Azerbaijan, after clashing with the Armenian Church.
culture: Armenia was the first country to adopt Christianity as a state religion, in 301, and its monasteries and unique alphabet, created in 405, are pillars of identity. Mount Ararat, now in Turkey, dominates the view from Yerevan and the national imagination. Duduk music, lavash bread and a huge global diaspora connect Armenians everywhere. The 1915 genocide is commemorated every 24 April.
society: Armenia lost Nagorno-Karabakh to Azerbaijan in 2023, and more than 100,000 Armenians fled. Pashinyan has moved away from Russia, freezing membership of its military alliance. Remittances, IT and re-exports to Russia have powered growth. His feud with the Church's leadership led to arrests of senior clergy.

story: In 2023, Azerbaijan took Nagorno-Karabakh in a lightning offensive and more than 100,000 ethnic Armenians fled a land their people had lived in for centuries. Russia, Armenia's treaty ally, whose peacekeepers were on the ground, did nothing. Since then, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, a former journalist who came to power in the peaceful 2018 Velvet Revolution, has bet his country's future on making peace with Azerbaijan and Turkey and turning toward the West. In June 2026, Armenians voted on that bet.

On 7 June, Pashinyan's Civil Contract won 49.8 percent, enough to govern alone for a third term (AP via KTLA). The runner-up, with 23.3 percent, was Strong Armenia, led by Samvel Karapetyan, a billionaire who made his fortune in Russia and spent the campaign under house arrest, accused of calling for the government's overthrow, a charge he calls political. Former president Robert Kocharyan's bloc took about 10 percent. Pashinyan fell short of the two-thirds he needs to change the constitution, which matters because Azerbaijan says it will not sign the peace treaty until Armenia drops constitutional language it sees as a claim on Karabakh (EVN Report). Trump endorsed Pashinyan before the vote. Moscow has answered Armenia's westward turn by banning imports of Armenian fruit, vegetables and milk. Analysts credited the win to the peace process and normalisation with Turkey, but also to pressure on public employees to back the ruling party (PISM).
briefing.power: A parliamentary republic since 2018. The prime minister leads the majority in the National Assembly, elected by proportional representation with a bonus to guarantee a stable majority; the president, elected by parliament, is ceremonial.
briefing.holders: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan (Civil Contract), in office since 2018.
